title: Samsung's HBM Market Share Jumps to 33%; Hybrid Bonding Technology Could Be Key to Overtaking Rivals
key_facts: Damnang (Korea), on 7 Oct, citing interviews with technical personnel, reported SK Hynix has had difficulties developing hybrid bonding for next-generation HBM while Samsung is reportedly already delivering samples using it.
The information is not from either company, and the report gives no HBM generation, stack layer count or customer.
SK Hynix said on 18 June it had delivered 12-layer HBM4E samples using its existing Advanced MR-MUF packaging, with 17% better thermal resistance than HBM4.
Samsung introduced its hybrid copper bonding (HCB) technology on 17 March, saying it should cut thermal resistance by over 20% versus thermocompression bonding.
Counterpoint Research: Samsung's HBM share rose from 21% in Q1 to 33% in Q2, with SK Hynix at 30%; SK Hynix's Q1 figure is on a shipment basis and its Q2 figure on a spending basis.
Sample delivery is not mass production; yield, cost and capacity decide commercial advantage.
quote_evidence: According to a report by South Korean tech media outlet Damnang on October 7, citing interviews with relevant technical personnel, SK Hynix has encountered difficulties in developing hybrid bonding technology for next-generation HBM, while Samsung Electronics is reportedly already delivering samples using the technology to customers.
However, the information does not come from official announcements by either company, and the report does not specify the HBM generation involved, stack layer count, or customer details.
According to Counterpoint Research data, Samsung's HBM market share rose from 21% in Q1 to 33% in Q2, pulling SK Hynix's share down to 30%.
why_it_matters_hint: One Korean report says Samsung is ahead of SK Hynix on a next-generation memory stacking method, but nothing is confirmed.
